mainTopic: סוכה המדובללת, two-layer סכך, and the rule of חבוט רמי
overview: The משנה rules that a סוכה that is מדובללת, and one whose shade is greater than its sun, is כשרה. It also rules that very thick סכך, so thick that stars cannot be seen through it, is כשרה. רב explains מדובללת as a sparse, 'poor' סוכה, and reads the first clause as one law. שמואל explains it as two layers of reeds, one up and one down, and reads the clause as two separate laws. אביי rules that two layers 3 טפחים apart are פסולה. רבא narrows this: if the upper layer is a טפח wide, it is כשרה because of חבוט רמי. רבא proves this from a משנה and a ברייתא about ceiling boards and corpse impurity. רב אשי then challenges the rule with a ברייתא about cross-beams over a מבוי, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A סוכה that is מדובללת with more shade than sun is כשרה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סוכה that is מדובללת, and whose shade is greater than its sun, is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סוכה that is מדובללת and whose shade is more than its sunlight is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule: a סוכה with this unusual kind of סכך is still כשרה, as long as the shade beats the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מדובללת is unclear, and the גמרא will soon ask what it means. The basic idea is that the סכך does not have to be neat or full. The key test is that the shade inside must be more than the sun.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text being explained)
An unclear word describing the סכך; the גמרא will define it
Its shade is greater than its sun
Kosher / valid

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A sukkah that is meduvlelet
and whose shade is greater than its sunlight
is kosher.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה that is מדובללת, and one whose shade is greater than its sun, is כשרה.

steps.title: Very thick roofing is still kosher
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that סכך as thick as a house roof, so that stars cannot be seen through it, is still כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סוכה whose roofing is thick like a house, even though the stars cannot be seen from inside it, is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule: even very thick סכך is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a סוכה must let you see the stars, so thick סכך would make it like a regular house. The משנה teaches that seeing the stars is not required. Very thick סכך is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick / dense
Like a kind of house
Stars

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 1. Step 1 is about סכך that is thin or unusual. This step is about סכך that is extra thick. Both cases are כשרה.

phrases.english: One that is thick like a kind of house,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכּוֹכָבִים נִרְאִין מִתּוֹכָהּ
phrases.english: even though the stars cannot be seen from inside it
is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְעוּבָּה כְּמִין בַּיִת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכּוֹכָבִים נִרְאִין מִתּוֹכָהּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thick סכך through which the stars cannot be seen is כשרה.

steps.title: What does מדובללת mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear word מדובללת in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking what the hard word in the משנה means. Two answers will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about a word, not a challenge. The way the word is defined will affect how the whole first line of the משנה is read.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
What is?

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is meduvlelet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה's first rule.

steps.title: רב: a poor, sparse סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that מדובללת means a 'poor' סוכה whose סכך is thin and sparse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It means a poor סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. מדובללת means a סוכה with thin, skimpy סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'poor' סוכה has sparse סכך with many small gaps, though no single gap is 3 טפחים. רב teaches that this is still כשרה, as long as the shade is more than the sun.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'poor' sukkah, with sparse סכך

phrases.english: Rav said:
A poor (sparse) sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 3.

steps.title: שמואל: one reed up, one reed down
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that מדובללת means סכך made of two layers. Each upper reed sits over a gap in the lower layer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: one reed goes up and one reed goes down.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer. מדובללת means the סכך is set up in two layers that cover each other's gaps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's case, each layer alone has gaps. Together they create shade, because the top reeds sit above the spaces in the bottom layer. The question this raises is whether the two layers can count together as one roof. אביי and רבא will discuss this.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed going up (upper layer)
A reed going down (lower layer)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
A reed going up and a reed going down.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: קָנֶה עוֹלֶה וְקָנֶה יוֹרֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing definition next to רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מדובללת means two layers of reeds that cover each other's gaps.

steps.title: רב reads the first clause as one law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב reads the משנה's first clause as a single law: a sparse סוכה is כשרה as long as the shade is more than the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב teaches one law, and שמואל teaches two. רב teaches one: a סוכה that is מדובללת. What is מדובללת? It is sparse. As long as its shade is more than its sun, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a contrast: רב and שמואל read the משנה's first line differently. It starts by showing רב's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'shade greater than sun' is the condition that makes the sparse סוכה כשרה. It is not a separate case. The phrase means: even though it is sparse, it is כשרה as long as there is more shade than sun.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches (it as) one law
He teaches (it as) two laws
Thin, sparse, dangling

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the three similar words. מדובללת is the word in the משנה. מדולדלת (sparse) is how רב explains it. מבולבלת (mixed up) is how שמואל explains it.

phrases.english: Rav teaches one,
and Shmuel teaches two.
Rav teaches one:
a sukkah that is meduvlelet,
what is meduvlelet? Sparse,
as long as its shade is greater than its sun, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב תָּנֵי חֲדָא, וּשְׁמוּאֵל תָּנֵי תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רב's definition shapes his reading of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a sparse סוכה is כשרה on condition that its shade is greater than its sun.

steps.title: שמואל reads the first clause as two separate laws
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, the משנה teaches two separate rulings: a mixed-up, two-layer סוכה is כשרה, and a סוכה whose shade is greater than its sun is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל teaches two. What is מדובללת? Mixed up. And the משנה teaches two things: a mixed-up סוכה is kosher, and one whose shade is more than its sun is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the contrast by showing שמואל's reading. In his view, the first line of the משנה contains two different laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the two-layer סוכה needs no 'shade beats sun' condition, since together the layers make full shade. The 'shade greater than sun' phrase is a separate case. It means a סוכה is כשרה even if some sun gets in, as long as shade is the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed up / disordered (reeds in two layers)
It (the משנה) teaches

steps.whatToRemember: רב: מדובללת means sparse, and 'shade beats sun' is its condition (one law). שמואל: מדובללת means two mixed-up layers, and 'shade beats sun' is a separate law (two laws).

phrases.english: And Shmuel teaches two:
what is meduvlelet? Mixed up,
and it teaches two things:
a mixed-up sukkah is kosher,
and one whose shade is greater than its sun is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל תָּנֵי תַּרְתֵּי: מַאי מְדוּבְלֶלֶת — מְבוּלְבֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the רב / שמואל contrast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, a two-layer mixed-up סוכה is כשרה, and separately, a סוכה whose shade is greater than its sun is כשרה.

steps.title: אביי: layers 3 handbreadths apart make it invalid
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits שמואל's two-layer case. It is כשרה only if the layers are less than 3 טפחים apart. If they are 3 טפחים apart, it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They only taught this when there are not 3 handbreadths between one layer and the other. But if there are 3 handbreadths between them, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to the rule that a two-layer סוכה is כשרה. The layers must be close together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two layers can count as one roof only if they are close enough to join. When the gap is 3 טפחים or more, they are seen as two separate roofs, and each one alone has gaps. Then the סוכה becomes פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) in the case of...
Between this one and that one (between the two layers)
Three handbreadths
Invalid

phrases.english: Abaye said: They did not teach this,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: except where there are not three handbreadths between one and the other,
but if there are, between one and the other,
three handbreadths, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on שמואל's two-layer case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A two-layer סוכה is כשרה only if the layers are less than 3 טפחים apart. Otherwise it is פסולה.

steps.title: רבא: a handbreadth-wide upper layer is pressed down
steps.stepSummary: רבא narrows אביי's ruling. Even with a 3-טפחים gap, the סוכה is פסולה only if the upper layer is less than a טפח wide. If the upper layer is a טפח wide, it is כשרה, because of the rule of חבוט רמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even when there are 3 handbreadths between them, we only said it is invalid when the upper roof is not a handbreadth wide. But if the upper roof is a handbreadth wide, it is kosher, because we say: 'press it down and cast it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to אביי's limit. A wide enough upper layer saves the סוכה even when the layers are far apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An upper layer that is a טפח wide counts as real, significant סכך. So we imagine it pressed down onto the lower layer, filling its gaps, and together they form one kosher roof. Only thin upper reeds, less than a טפח, stay separate and make the סוכה פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said (this) when...
Its (upper) roof is a handbreadth wide
'Press down and cast': we view the upper layer as pressed down onto the lower one

steps.whyThisMatters: חבוט רמי is a key halachic tool. It lets סכך at different heights count as one roof when the upper part is significant (at least a טפח).
steps.whatToRemember: Two-layer סכך: less than 3 טפחים apart is כשרה. 3 טפחים or more apart is פסולה (אביי), unless the upper layer is a טפח wide, in which case it is כשרה through חבוט רמי (רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
phrases.english: Even if there are three handbreadths between one and the other,
we also only said this (that it is invalid),
when its upper roof is not a handbreadth wide,
but if its upper roof is a handbreadth wide, it is kosher.
For we say: press it down and cast it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a 3-טפחים gap, a two-layer סוכה is כשרה if the upper layer is a טפח wide, because of חבוט רמי.

steps.title: רבא asks where his rule comes from
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks himself: what is my source that חבוט רמי applies only when the upper layer is a טפח wide?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I know that when it has a טפח we say 'knock it down and place it,' and when it does not have a טפח we do not say 'knock it down and place it'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks where his own rule comes from. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule from step 9 has two sides. With a טפח of width we use חבוט רמי, and without a טפח we do not. He now promises a source that supports both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (the speaker introduces his own source)
'Knock it down and place it.' We picture the upper layer as pushed down to the level of the lower layer.
A handbreadth (about 8–10 cm)

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it
that when it has a handbreadth
we say 'knock it down and place it,'
and when it does not have it
we do not say 'knock it down and place it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא opens a proof for the ruling he gave in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the rule that חבוט רמי depends on the upper layer being a טפח wide.

steps.title: The משנה about ceiling boards and corpse impurity
steps.stepSummary: A משנה describes two layers of ceiling boards. When the upper boards sit over the gaps between the lower boards, impurity under any board spreads under all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The boards of a house and of its upper story have no plaster on them. If the boards are lined up one above the other, and impurity is under one of the lower boards, only what is beneath it is impure. If the impurity is between the lower and upper boards, only what is between them is impure. If it is on top of the upper board, everything above it up to the sky is impure. If the upper boards sit over the gaps between the lower boards, and impurity is under them, then everything under all of them is impure. If the impurity is on top of them, everything above it up to the sky is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a משנה about corpse impurity spreading under a roof. It shows the idea of 'pushing down' the upper boards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the upper boards are directly above the lower boards, each board is its own separate roof. When the upper boards sit over the gaps, the משנה pictures them as pushed down to fill the gaps, making one solid ceiling. That is why impurity under one board spreads 'under all of them.' This is exactly the idea of חבוט רמי.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Beams or boards
Plaster or packed covering that joins the boards together
Lined up directly one above the other
Ritual impurity (here, from a corpse spreading under a roof)
All the way up to the sky

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not about סוכה at all. It is about corpse impurity under a roof (טומאת אהל). רבא borrows the 'push it down' principle from these laws and applies it to סכך.

phrases.english: As we learned:
the boards of the house and the upper story
that have no plaster on them,
and they are lined up one above the other:
if impurity is beneath one of them,
what is beneath it is impure.
If it is between the lower and the upper board,
what is between them is impure.
If it is on top of the upper board,
what is above it up to the sky is impure.
If the upper boards were over the gaps between the lower boards,
and impurity is beneath them,
what is beneath all of them is impure.
If it is on top of them,
what is above them up to the sky is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the first part of the source that רבא promised in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that חבוט רמי exists, meaning upper boards can be viewed as pushed down into the gaps.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about ceiling boards of a house and its upper story.

steps.title: The ברייתא adds the טפח requirement
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on this משנה says the 'under all is impure' rule applies only when the boards are a טפח wide and the gaps between them are a טפח wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught on this משנה: When is this said? When the boards are a טפח wide and there is an opening of a טפח between them. But if there is no opening of a טפח between them, and impurity is under one of them, only what is beneath it is impure. What is between the layers and on top of them is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא that explains the משנה adds a condition. The 'push it down' picture works only when the boards have a טפח of width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are בזמן שיש בהן טפח, meaning 'when the boards are a טפח wide.' Only then do we treat the upper boards as pushed down to join the lower ones. This gives רבא the missing piece: the width of a טפח is what allows חבוט רמי.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא was taught commenting on it
In what case is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
An open space of a טפח, the minimum size for impurity to spread through
Pure

phrases.english: And it was taught on it:
In what case are these words said?
When they are a handbreadth wide
and between them is an opening of a handbreadth.
But if there is no opening of a handbreadth between them,
and impurity is beneath one of them,
what is beneath it is impure;
what is between them and on top of them is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This adds a condition to the משנה from step 11, which completes רבא's source.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that חבוט רמי requires the boards to be a טפח wide.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא commenting on the משנה about ceiling boards.

steps.title: So חבוט רמי needs a טפח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the conclusion: with a טפח of width we say חבוט רמי, and without it we do not. The proof works.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that when it has a טפח, we say 'knock it down and place it.' When it does not have a טפח, we do not say 'knock it down and place it.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what the ברייתא proves and accepts רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same idea that makes impurity spread under all the boards also makes a two-layer סכך count as one layer. Since that idea depends on a טפח of width, רבא's ruling for סוכה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, we see that
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: חבוט רמי means picturing the upper layer as pushed down to the lower one. It applies only when the upper layer is at least a טפח wide. The source is the laws of טומאת אהל.

phrases.english: Evidently, when it has a handbreadth,
we say 'knock it down and place it,'
and when it does not have a handbreadth,
we do not say 'knock it down and place it'!
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This draws the conclusion from the משנה and ברייתא and answers רבא's question from step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חבוט רמי applies only when the upper layer is a טפח wide, which confirms רבא's ruling.

steps.title: רב אשי questions whether this is always true
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא repeats רבא's teaching. רב אשי asks him: is it really true that whenever there is less than a טפח, we never say חבוט רמי?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא sat and taught this teaching. רב אשי said to רב כהנא: And is it true that anywhere it does not have a טפח, we do not say 'knock it down and place it'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא repeats רבא's rule, and רב אשי pushes back against it. This sets up a challenge that the גמרא will develop next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי is not questioning the basic idea of חבוט רמי. He is questioning the second half of the rule, that less than a טפח never allows it. The words 'anywhere' (וכל היכא) suggest he knows a case where we do push down something narrower than a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Sat (in the study hall, teaching)
A teaching or halachic ruling
And is it so in every case where...?

phrases.english: Rav Kahana sat
and was teaching this ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
And is it so that anywhere it does not have a handbreadth
we do not say 'knock it down and place it'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ טֶפַח לָא אָמְרִינַן חֲבוֹט רְמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the negative half of the rule that step 13 just confirmed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חבוט רמי never applies when the upper layer is less than a טפח wide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'anywhere' hints that there are cases where something narrower than a טפח is still treated as pushed down, so the rule may be too broad.

steps.title: רב אשי quotes a ברייתא about beams that do not reach across an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: To back up his challenge, רב אשי starts quoting a ברייתא about a cross-beam (קורה) over a מבוי. If the beam, or two beams from opposite walls, leave a gap of less than three טפחים, no extra beam is needed. If the gap is three, another beam is needed. Then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל begins to give his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: A beam that sticks out from one wall of the alleyway and does not touch the other wall, and also two beams, one sticking out from this wall and one from that wall, that do not touch each other: if the gap is less than three טפחים, you do not need to bring another beam. If it is three, you need to bring another beam. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to quote the source behind רב אשי's challenge to רבא. This passage is only the opening of the ברייתא. It sets up the case that will be used against רבא on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי can be fixed for carrying on שבת with a קורה across its entrance. Here the beam does not fully span the gap, but a gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed through לבוד. A gap of three breaks it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds that לבוד works up to four טפחים, is about to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a source used against what was just said)
A cross-beam placed over the entrance of an alleyway to allow carrying on שבת
An alleyway shared by several courtyards
A wall
Rule that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as if it were closed
A תנא who holds that the gap-closing rule reaches up to four טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: This opening part of the ברייתא is about לבוד (closing a sideways gap), not yet about חבוט רמי (pushing a layer down). Don't look for רב אשי's punch here yet. The ברייתא is being quoted in full, and the case that challenges רבא comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that רב אשי brings for his challenge.

phrases.english: A beam that projects from this wall
and does not touch that (opposite) wall,
and similarly, two beams,
one projecting from this wall
and one projecting from that wall
and they do not touch each other,
if the gap is less than three handbreadths,
phrases.notes: A gap that small counts as closed, because of לבוד.

phrases.english: one need not bring another beam;
if it is three, one must bring another beam.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud (he holds that לבוד works up to four)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא behind רב אשי's question in Step 14, which challenged רבא's conclusion in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that without a טפח of width we never say חבוט רמי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא (in its continuation) will apply a merging or pushing-down principle to beams even without a טפח, which would contradict רבא
